subject: Redwood integration: post-call recap & next steps
messages:
From: Marissa Cole <marissa@redwood.com>
To: Alex Johnson <alex.johnson@acme.com>
Cc: Vivek Kulkarni <vivek@redwood.com>, Neha Kapoor <neha@redwood.com>
Date: Mon, 30 Nov 2026 15:02:00 -0800
Subject: Redwood integration: post-call recap & next steps

Alex — thanks again for taking the time today. Quick recap from our call and proposed next steps so we’re all aligned.

High-level pain points you shared:
- Cost per inference is too high for nightly re-ranking jobs and interactive search traffic.
- Latency spikes during peak business hours (affects UX).
- Need deterministic structured outputs for downstream analytics pipeline (JSON schema).
- Want streaming partial responses for long-form assistant flows and function-based orchestration to call downstream systems.
- Goal: replace current endpoint + custom caching with an embeddings + reranking pipeline to improve relevance while controlling cost.

Product/technical fit we discussed:
- SDKs: Python + JS SDKs support incremental streaming responses; minimal code changes required. We expect ~1-2 files of inference integration (client + streaming handler).
- Function calling: Redwood supports structured function calling; we can deserialize the model output into the function schema you need (we can iterate on schema today).
- Streaming: supports partial tokens + chunked structured outputs (we can send structured JSON chunks as they finish).
- Embeddings + reranking: we recommend using embeddings for candidate retrieval and Redwood’s reranker for top-K scoring to reduce cold token generation costs.
- Caching & batching: prefix caching and workload-aware batching should reduce token spend for repeated queries.

Attachments: I’m attaching a short integration notes PDF and our SOC 2 summary for your security team.

Proposed next steps:
1) Technical deep-dive with your eng team (60m) — walkthrough SDK code sample and function-calling schema. Suggested times: Wed 12:00-13:00 PT or Thu 09:00-10:00 PT.
2) We’ll provision a short POC key (14 days, limited tokens) and a sample reranking config for your dataset.
3) Security/compliance: send us the security questionnaire (happy to loop Neha for answers).
4) Follow-on: propose a phased rollout plan (POC -> canary -> prod) and an optional Dedicated pool if you want predictable throughput.

Let me know which slot works and I’ll send a calendar invite + code snippet ahead of the call.

—
Marissa Cole
Enterprise Account Executive, Redwood Inference
marissa@redwood.com
+1 (415) 555-0123

Attachments:
- redwood-integration-notes.pdf (stub)
- SOC2-summary.pdf (stub)

From: Alex Johnson <alex.johnson@acme.com>
To: Marissa Cole <marissa@redwood.com>
Cc: Vivek Kulkarni <vivek@redwood.com>, Neha Kapoor <neha@redwood.com>
Date: Mon, 30 Nov 2026 15:45:00 -0800
Subject: Re: Redwood integration: post-call recap & next steps

Thanks Marissa — that all looks good. A few clarifications from our side: 

- Priority ranking: 1) Embeddings + reranking (reduce cost, improve relevance), 2) streaming for agent UX, 3) structured JSON output for analytics.
- SDK compatibility: our platform uses Node + a small Python microservice for batch jobs. Are the streaming + function-calling examples available in both language SDKs?
- Function-calling schema: we need the model to return exactly the fields in our ingestion schema (id, rank_score, canonical_text, metadata.{source,timestamp}). Can you share an example JSON schema we can iterate on?
- Security: attaching our security questionnaire (acme-security-questions.pdf). We’ll need SOC 2 details and data residency notes for EU customers (we might move some data).

Happy to take Wed 12:00 PT for the technical deep-dive. Please send an invite and a short code sample for Node streaming + function call so my engs can skim before the call.

—
Alex Johnson
Head of Search Platform, Acme Analytics
alex.johnson@acme.com

Attachment: acme-security-questions.pdf (stub)

From: Vivek Kulkarni <vivek@redwood.com>
To: Alex Johnson <alex.johnson@acme.com>, Marissa Cole <marissa@redwood.com>
Cc: Neha Kapoor <neha@redwood.com>
Date: Mon, 30 Nov 2026 16:30:00 -0800
Subject: Re: Redwood integration: post-call recap & next steps (pricing + POC)

Alex — quick follow from the pricing/eng ops side. Appreciate the priorities — here’s what we can do to make the POC low-friction: 

- POC offer: 14-day sandbox key with 200k tokens + access to our small reranker model and embeddings endpoint. Rough estimate for production: $0.03-0.06 per 1k tokens depending on batching + quantization profile; reranker priced per 1k calls. We’ll provide a detailed estimate after we see the query distribution.
- Dedicated vs hosted: for predictable throughput at scale we recommend Dedicated (monthly commit) but you can run the POC on hosted API and we’ll help shape autoscaling policies.
- Compliance: Marissa/Neha will reply to the security questionnaire — we can provide SOC 2 report and outline EU region availability and data residency options.

Marissa — sending the Node streaming + function-calling snippet and a sample JSON schema (short) in a follow-up message to include in the invite.

Vivek
Director, Solutions Engineering, Redwood Inference
vivek@redwood.com

From: Marissa Cole <marissa@redwood.com>
To: Alex Johnson <alex.johnson@acme.com>
Cc: Vivek Kulkarni <vivek@redwood.com>, Neha Kapoor <neha@redwood.com>
Date: Mon, 30 Nov 2026 17:20:00 -0800
Subject: Re: Redwood integration: post-call recap & next steps

Perfect — Wed 12:00 PT confirmed. Invite sent with video link and a short pre-read (Node streaming example + function-calling JSON schema). Copying the key items below so your team can prep quickly.

Quick pre-read highlights:
- Node streaming example: client.on('data', chunk => parseChunk(chunk)); we include a helper to coalesce structured JSON chunks into final object.
- Function-calling example: model returns a JSON payload matching your ingestion schema; Redwood can validate types and return an error object if required fields are missing.
- Reranking flow: retrieve candidates (your vector store), call /rerank with top-50 candidates, use returned rank_score to reorder, only generate full text for top-5 to save cost.

I’ll follow up after the call with the POC key and a sample reranker config based on your dataset size. If anything changes for the Wed slot, let me know ASAP.

Thanks — looking forward to it.

—
Marissa Cole
Enterprise Account Executive, Redwood Inference
marissa@redwood.com
